I take women’s rights seriously, so this is one of the first things I asked about while visiting Ghardaïa, Algeria  Now this is not necessarily for any reason. It has nothing to do with religion or location. The only thing it has to do with is that many communities that are small and follow old traditions typically give less rights and protections to women. However, I was pleasantly surprised that this is not the case in Ghardaia.   I really appreciate what I learned about  Mozabite communities, giving women in their own committees and ability to make decisions for themselves. When it comes to dress, extra protections, to feel safe and comfortable in their marriages, and the community standing in solidarity with its women. Inside a traditional Kabylie home in the mountains of Northern Algeria 🇩🇿 Kabylie is home to Algeria’s Amazigh people, and getting to step inside one of these homes gave me a glimpse into a way of life that has been passed down for generations. What makes these homes so unique is how they were traditionally built around everyday life, with livestock kept on the lower level and the family living above them. One of the most unique homes I’ve ever seen. 🇩🇿 #algeria #kabyle #solotravel #amazigh #kabylie
